title: Does Noise Affect Concentration?
context:
Hannah: Thanks for running the pilot, Ravi. I know it took you all afternoon. How did it go?
Ravi: Mixed. We only needed twelve people for the pilot, but just five replied to our email. I think the subject line was boring.
Hannah: Ah. And the room? I booked the quiet lab.
Ravi: Someone else was already in there when we arrived, so we had to move to the seminar room.
Hannah: Annoying. And the questionnaire?
Ravi: Question six confused everyone. Half of them asked what moderately distracted meant.
Hannah: Okay, I'll reword it. What about the consent forms?
Ravi: Three people forgot to sign theirs and left before I noticed.
Hannah: Oh no. And the timer software?
Ravi: It crashed halfway through twice, so I had to restart the whole session. People turning up late wasn't a problem, though. Everyone was on time.
Hannah: Good. Let's see what Dr Chen thinks of the design.
Dr Chen: I've read it. Participants first. You plan twenty. That's too few for the effect you want, so I'd go for forty.
Hannah: Forty? We'd run out of time.
Dr Chen: Thirty-five is workable, but aim for forty. Now the noise. You're using pop music, but people differ in taste, which muddies the results. Use recordings of traffic instead.
Ravi: And the written summaries are graded by me.
Dr Chen: Since you know which condition each person was in, you could be biased. Ask a second marker to look at them too. Also, you only have noisy conditions. Add a silent one so you can compare.
Hannah: Should we pay the participants?
Dr Chen: Not necessary. Course credit is enough. One last thing. The task is twenty minutes long. That's tiring, and people will make mistakes because of fatigue, not noise. Ten minutes is plenty.
Ravi: Right, ten minutes.
Hannah: Now, analysis. I suggest the spreadsheet. We all know it already, so no training is needed.
Ravi: True. But the statistical package can cope with big datasets, and ours could reach hundreds of rows, so that's the sensible choice if the numbers grow.
Hannah: Is it on the lab computers?
Ravi: No, sadly. We'd have to install it on our laptops.
Hannah: Okay. What about the online calculator some people use?
Ravi: It costs nothing, which is attractive, but I wouldn't use it for the final analysis.
Hannah: And doing it by hand?
Ravi: Slow, but you'd get a very precise answer because you check every step. I'd keep that as a check. Then there's the chart app. It makes the graphs for you automatically, which would save us a whole night.
Dr Chen: Let's agree deadlines. The ethics form has to be with the committee by Friday.
Ravi: I thought it was Monday.
Dr Chen: The committee meets on Monday, so you submit it by Friday. Have all the sessions booked by next Monday. I need your draft report two weeks from now.
Hannah: And the poster? We could do it when the results are ready.
Dr Chen: No, I want a fixed date. It's due at the end of the month. The presentation itself is after the holidays, but finish the slides before they start.
Ravi: Understood. Thank you. It was useful to see everything go wrong before the real experiment.
Dr Chen: Exactly what a pilot is for. Email me if anything is unclear before the weekend.

questions.prompt: Which problem occurred when recruiting volunteers?
questions.why: Chỉ năm người trả lời email trong khi cần mười hai.
questions.quote: just five replied to our email

questions.prompt: Which problem occurred with the quiet lab?

questions.quote: Someone else was already in there

questions.prompt: Which problem occurred with the questionnaire?
questions.why: Câu sáu làm mọi người bối rối.

questions.prompt: Which problem occurred with the consent forms?
questions.why: Ba người quên ký rồi bỏ đi.

questions.prompt: Which problem occurred with the timer software?

questions.prompt: What does Dr Chen recommend for the number of participants?
options: Use traffic sounds instead of music
Have a second person mark them
questions.why: Hai mươi là quá ít; Dr Chen khuyên nhắm tới bốn mươi (ba mươi lăm vẫn làm được).

questions.prompt: What does Dr Chen recommend for the type of noise?
options: Use traffic sounds instead of music
Have a second person mark them

questions.prompt: What does Dr Chen recommend for the grading of the summaries?
options: Use traffic sounds instead of music
Have a second person mark them

questions.why: Ravi biết điều kiện của từng người nên có thể thiên vị; nhờ người chấm thứ hai.
questions.quote: Ask a second marker to look at them too

options: Use traffic sounds instead of music
Have a second person mark them
questions.why: Chỉ có điều kiện ồn; thêm điều kiện yên lặng để so sánh.

questions.prompt: What does Dr Chen recommend for the length of the task?

questions.why: Hai mươi phút gây mệt; mười phút là đủ. Bẫy: trả tiền người tham gia bị bác, tín chỉ khoá học là đủ.
